entries.text: GCC keeps an FP operation before the FPSR read that follows it in program order (GCC has no FENV_ACCESS).
entries.removed_by: no gate yet: not compiler correctness: GCC is allowed to reorder. Closing rule: FPSR read through an operation the compiler must order (asm with FP operand dependency), then gate on objects

entries.text: Host code between guest instructions (imports, native bodies) runs with the guest FPSR parked or raises nothing the guest sees.
entries.removed_by: planned: item 29 fact (L3a, w7). Windows model at the import boundary: imports run under the caller's rounding mode, set on both paths if the census shows a non-nearest mode at any import call site, and the callee's FPSR cumulative bits are ORed into the guest sticky state if a sticky read is reachable after the return. Native bodies run under the guest FPCR.

entries.text: An MMX read of a register popped by a static-stack function, with no MMX write since, reads data undefined on the CPU too.
entries.removed_by: no gate yet: the CPU value is defined (old bits); closing = write back on pop or prove no such read statically

entries.text: Every guest thread starts with FCW 0x027F and MXCSR 0x1F80.
entries.removed_by: planned: rt/enter.cc:46 sets FCW/MXCSR at thread reset; remaining: a call-graph check that no other path starts a guest thread

entries.text: The CONTEXT image handed to guest SEH handlers is only read back by the runtime restore, which restores a reachable control state.
entries.removed_by: no gate yet: a handler may write the FP control words in CONTEXT; being checked against rt/seh.c with the FP-mask fact

entries.text: With --eip fixed: semantics is translation-invariant in eip.
entries.removed_by: planned: mode to delete; A-EIPRANGE (symbolic eip) is the only product path

entries.text: Decoding (operand structure, family) is a function of the shape: masked imm/disp fields never change it.
entries.removed_by: planned: same decoder-agreement gate, run on every occurrence (not the representative): operand structure of each occurrence equals that of its shape

entries.text: For shapes outside the Sail model (x87 control/state, cpuid, rdtsc, part of SIMD: 7 019 shapes have no DSL builder yet) the reference is a transcription of the SDM compared with the host.
entries.removed_by: planned: no SDM transcription is a reference (orchestrator 2026-11-12). Shapes outside ACL2 x86isa get a census: closure-unreachable shapes drop out, and the orchestrator decides the reachable ones; forms are derived from the pinned model only

entries.text: 17 (mnemonic, undefined flag) pairs: the value the reference CPU produces is not yet pinned.
